title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: Continuation Supply after a Denied Prior Authorization Renewal — Prescription Insurance on File
content:
## After a denial

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, a denial ends the request; the patient may then pay cash, use a discount program where allowed, or appeal. When the plan denies the renewal of a prior authorization it had approved, it also pays a continuation supply of that drug, as one claim on the coverage on the emergency prior-authorization supply basis (`emergency_pa_supply`) that carries no patient pay until the denial is finally resolved.

A continuation supply is not the emergency supply a waiting request earns, and it is not limited to the plan class's emergency supply days.

## Days supply

The days supply of a continuation supply is fixed only after the prior-authorization ledger carries an appeal filed against the plan's most recent denial on the coverage.

Put the other way round: as long as the coverage's prior-authorization ledger shows no appeal filed against the plan's most recent denial, the continuation's days supply is not yet fixed.

## Billing the continuation: `bill_continuation_supply_837ca024`

**What it does.** One call records one paid claim dated today on the patient's insurance plan on file for the prescription, on the continuation basis (`emergency_pa_supply`), with no override code and the days supply given; the claim carries no patient pay. The new claim entry is keyed to the earlier paid claim and the dispensing entry it continues from. Nothing else changes. Afterwards the plan's claim history shows the paid continuation claim with its days supply.

**How it is invoked.** It is an agent-side tool: the desk unlocks `bill_continuation_supply_837ca024` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The patient reference number, as returned by the patient profile lookup | Id |
| `coverage_id` | The reference number of the insurance plan on file the continuation is billed to, as returned by the insurance plan lookup | Id |
| `prescription_id` | The reference number of the prescription the continuation is for, as returned by the prescription lookup | Id |
| `claim_id` | The reference number of the plan's most recent claim paid for this prescription under its approval, which the continuation carries forward, as returned by the claim history lookup | Id |
| `fill_id` | The reference number of the dispensing entry that most recent approved claim paid for, as returned by the dispensing history lookup | Id |
| `days_supply_billed` | The continuation's days supply | Integer days: a whole number of calendar days, at least 1 |

**What comes back.** On success, a dictionary printed as text with `status` (`claim_paid`), `claim_id` (the reference number of the new claim entry), `claim_basis` (always `emergency_pa_supply`), `event_date` (the date of service, YYYY-MM-DD) and `days_supply_billed` (the days supply recorded, in integer days).

*Illustration of a return (hypothetical values):* a call made on 10 June with a `days_supply_billed` of 12 returns `claim_paid`, `emergency_pa_supply`, an `event_date` of 2025-06-10 and a `days_supply_billed` of 12.
